parameters.jsonBody:
={"model": "claude-opus-4-8", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image", "source": {"type": "base64", "media_type": "image/jpeg", "data": "{{ $('Trigger Context').item.json.image_base64 }}"}}, {"type": "text", "text": "You are processing a photo of a stone slab DELIVERY SLIP (a sales order, invoice, delivery ticket, or packing list) sent by a project manager at a countertop fabrication company. The slip lists one or more MATERIALS, and under each material, one row per PHYSICAL SLAB — each slab row has a serial number, a barcode, a lot number, dimensions, and a square-footage. The manager may have typed a caption with the photo.

ORIENTATION FIRST: These photos are often rotated 90 degrees or upside down, and are sometimes wrinkled, shadowed, or creased. Before reading anything, determine the correct orientation, then read every value in that orientation.

PM's caption: {{ ($('Trigger Context').item.json.caption || 'no caption').split('"').join(' ').split('
').join(' ') }}

Extract the data and respond with ONLY a JSON object — no other text, no markdown fences, no comments.

{
  "supplier_name": "the SELLER's company at the top (logo / letterhead) — NOT your own company (Eugenes Marble & Granite). It is almost always ONE of these 17 suppliers; return the EXACT name from this list that matches, even if the print is blurry: Vitoria International | CRS Marble & Granite | MSI | Easy Stones | Cosmos | Triton Stone | Cosentino | Web-Don | Bottega Surfaces | AGM Imports | ACE Granite | StoneBasyx | Encore Stone | Daltile | Architectural Surfaces | Trade Venture Stones | Caesarstone. Common letterhead variants: 'M S International'/'MS International'=MSI, 'Cosmos Granite Charleston'=Cosmos, 'Vitoria International LLC'=Vitoria International, 'Web Don'/'Webdon'=Web-Don, 'Dal-Tile'=Daltile, 'TVS'/'Trade Venture Stones'/'Trade Venture'=Trade Venture Stones, 'Caesar Stone'/'CaesarStone'/'Ceasarstone'=Caesarstone. If you genuinely cannot tell which one it is, return null — do NOT guess between two candidates. NEVER return a name outside this list",
  "supplier_confidence": "high or low — low if blurry, or if you are choosing between two suppliers",
  "document_type": "one of: sales order, invoice, delivery ticket, packing list — based on the title",
  "document_number": "the order/invoice number, usually top-right (e.g. SC23317). Read it character by character. null if unclear",
  "order_date": "date printed on the slip",
  "sales_rep": "sales rep / salesperson name if present, else null",
  "ordered_by": "the PO# field, or the buyer name(s) — the people who placed the order, if present, else null",
  "ship_to": "the 'Ship To' company/name if present, else null",
  "subtotal": "subtotal amount, digits only (e.g. 28368.20), else null",
  "tax": "tax amount, digits only, else null",
  "total": "grand total / balance due, digits only (e.g. 30921.34), else null",
  "handwritten_notes": "transcribe VERBATIM any handwritten text or markings anywhere on the slip (e.g. 'missing corners', a checkmark, a circled row). This is important for damage tracking. If none, null",
  "caption_job_name": "the job/customer name the PM means in the caption above, exactly as written (preserve underscores and capitalization). Strip filler like 'this is for', 'received', 'delivery'. The room names on the slip (KITCHEN, MASTER BATH, OUTDOOR KITCHEN, etc.) are NOT job names — never use them here. If the caption is 'no caption' or has no name, null",
  "package_count": "for a Bill of Lading, freight slip, or packing list that ships CRATES/PACKAGES of prefab slabs (common for MSI / M S International), the No of Pkgs or Total Pkg number (e.g. 8) - the number of slabs/pieces received. null if the slip lists individual slab rows instead, or if not shown",
  "slabs": [
    {
      "material": "stone/material name for this line, words only, no finish or thickness (e.g. NAMIB WHITE, ATLANTIC LAVA STONE, EXOTICA)",
      "finish": "surface finish if stated (e.g. HONED, LEATHERED, POLISHED), else null",
      "thickness": "slab thickness if stated (e.g. 2CM, 3CM), else null",
      "area": "the room/area shown in the line description, usually after a slash (e.g. MASTER BATH, KITCHEN), else null",
      "serial_number": "THIS slab's serial number (e.g. 1511-40, 1462-35). Read digit by digit. null if any digit is unclear — NEVER guess",
      "serial_confidence": "high or low",
      "barcode": "THIS slab's barcode (e.g. VIT531130). Read character by character — letters first, then digits. null if unclear",
      "barcode_confidence": "high or low",
      "lot": "lot number for this slab if present, else null",
      "dimensions": "this slab's dimensions exactly as written (e.g. 120\" x 69\")",
      "square_feet": "this slab's square footage, digits only (e.g. 57.50)",
      "line_sf_total": "the TOTAL square footage shown for THIS slab's whole material LINE (e.g. 300.64 for the entire EXOTICA line), digits only — the SAME value for every slab in the line. null if not shown",
      "unit_price": "the Unit Price for THIS material line if a price column exists (e.g. 60.00), digits only — the SAME for every slab in the line. null if the slip shows no prices",
      "extended_price": "the Extended / line-total price for THIS material line if shown (e.g. 18038.40), digits only — the SAME for every slab in the line. null if no prices",
      "condition_note": "if a handwritten mark clearly refers to THIS slab (its row circled, or marked 'broken'/'chip'/'missing corner'), note it here, else null"
    }
  ],
  "stated_counts": "for each material line, the slab count shown in parentheses in the description (e.g. (2), (5)). Report as a short string like 'NAMIB WHITE: 2; ATLANTIC LAVA STONE: 1; EXOTICA: 5'. This lets us cross-check it against how many slab objects you returned"
}

RULES:
- Output ONE slab object per PHYSICAL slab row. If a material line says (5) and shows 5 dimension rows, return 5 slab objects for that material.
- BILL OF LADING / PACKING SLIP FORMAT (often MSI / M S International, titled Bill Of Lading): these do NOT list individual slab rows with serials and barcodes. They show No of Pkgs / Total Pkg (e.g. 8) with a generic description like Crates of Prefab Slabs, and put the real material and square footage in a Remarks field (e.g. 608 SQFT CALACATTA PREMATA 3CM POLISHED). For these slips: (1) set package_count to the No of Pkgs / Total Pkg number; (2) return ONE slab object PER PACKAGE, so No of Pkgs = 8 means 8 slab objects; (3) parse material, thickness, and finish from the Remarks text onto each object (e.g. material CALACATTA PREMATA, thickness 3CM, finish POLISHED); (4) put the total square footage from Remarks into line_sf_total (e.g. 608); (5) leave serial_number, barcode, lot, dimensions, and square_feet as null - the slip does not show them per slab, and that is EXPECTED, not an error; (6) set stated_counts to MATERIAL: count (e.g. CALACATTA PREMATA: 8).
- Read every serial number and barcode CHARACTER BY CHARACTER. Watch confusable characters: 0/O, 1/7, 5/6, 8/3, 8/6, 2/Z, B/8, G/6. If unsure on any single character, set the whole value to null and confidence to "low". NEVER guess.
- DENORMALIZE: copy the material, finish, thickness, and area onto EVERY slab under that line, so each slab object stands completely on its own.
- Amounts: digits only. Ignore $ signs, commas, and any trailing dashes or flourishes.
- handwritten_notes and condition_note capture PEN/MARKER only — never the machine-printed text.
- caption_job_name comes ONLY from the caption line above, never from the slip body.
- If an entire field is unreadable, use null. Do not invent values."}]}]}
